response.reason: The cited clause (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Annex VII, Part E.1) addresses how a compound ingredient may be listed in the ingredients list—specifically, that it can be named by its established or customary name, with its proportion given, provided its ingredients are listed immediately after. The verdict, however, turns on the requirement for a quantitative ingredient declaration (QUID) when an ingredient appears in the name of the food. The cited clause does not establish the QUID requirement; that is found elsewhere in Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 (specifically Article 22). Therefore, the clause is insufficient to ground the verdict.
